chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'adah ibn Sadah, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): He was asked about a man who slaughters [an animal] and the knife moves quickly, causing the head to be severed, so he said: 'The slaughter is valid; there is no harm in eating it, provided he did not intend that.'
ai.seo_question: Is an animal's slaughter valid if the knife cuts off its head in one quick motion?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the validity of slaughter depends on the intentionality of the act rather than the mechanical precision of the cut, establishing the principle of 'al-dhakāh al-wahīyah' (the singular, decisive cut). This ruling distinguishes between a swift, natural motion which is permissible and a deliberate, excessive action that might invalidate the process, reflecting the Shia emphasis on intent (niyyah) in ritual purity. The narration underscores the flexibility in fiqh regarding physical execution as long as the core requirement of a conscious, single severing is met without deliberate deviation.
